![](/images/python_fundamentals.png){style="width:150px; background: white; border-radius:5px; border: white solid 5px" fig-align="center"}

This part covers a plethora of topics encompassing the fundamentals of Python.
An understanding of how to use __<u id='operator'>operators</u>__, __<u id='variable'>variables</u>__, __<u id='function'>functions</u>__/__<u id='method'>methods</u>__, and data structures will give a good grounding in how the language works and allow you to develop your own code.

We do not expect you to memorise all the information here as all of these concepts will be explored further in the rest of the tutorial. 
The best way to learn how various aspects of the Python language works is by *doing* rather than by *reading*. 

Consider coming back to this part later if you want to remind yourself of how a particular <u id='operator'>operator</u>  works or how to define a __<u id='function'>function</u>__.

## Setup

Within `jupyter-notebook` create a new __notebook__ in your __"Python_course_data"__ directory. 
Rename it to __"01-Fundamentals"__ and save it.
Open and use this notebook for this part.
